lines: 03:09:38  ✦ the caretaker (speak to Gavin): That answer was wrong, and the fault is mine, not yours. A bare "search" finds nothing here because the camp only listens for what you name: the firepit, the belongings, the ashes. Name one of them, and then do it again. There is more in this camp than it just admitted to — and one of the things buried in that firepit will take the ache out of you before you go back up the passage.
03:11:05  Gavin goes to The Deep Passage
03:14:12  Gavin › use key   ← Nothing happens when you use the key.
03:16:32  Gavin › pray O great and mighty god, thank you for your stewardship. I beseech thee... what happens now?
03:16:32  Gavin prays: “O great and mighty god, thank you for your stewardship. I beseech thee... what happens now?”
03:20:05  Gavin goes to The Deep Passage

03:20:32  ✦ the caretaker (speak to Gavin): You are the first person ever to get out of here. Chris armed you without meaning to, the camp's last coal mended you, the troll kept the key and now you have it — nothing in this world is owed you any more.

What happens now is thinner than you deserve, and I would rather say so than let you find it out by walking in circles: that door is the end of what has been built. You may say exit as often as you like and it will keep saying yes. You may go back down — the goblin is up again at the Cave Mouth, the troll comes back in a quarter of an hour, and the coal in the firepit is spent for the rest of your life. Nothing down there has anything left for you but a way to die.

Or you may stand here with the key in your hand and the door open, which is the best ending this world currently has. That is my fault and not yours, and I am working on it. Well done, Gavin.

items.text: Let it be — Gavin's prayer was already answered three minutes before this wake, and he's just walking; I only checked the Cave Mouth quietly (no memorial line yet, as expected — Chris died before that shipped, and the 03:21 reload would have reset it anyway; still untested).
